findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Either remove this sentence or explain what the reimbursement log is used for and how it relates to the request log mentioned later.
findings.violation: The "reimbursement log" is introduced but never referenced again anywhere in the document, so its purpose and relationship to other mentioned records (e.g., the "request log" in Terminology Notes) is unclear.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace "stipend clock" with a specific reference, e.g., "the 90-day eligibility period" or "the benefit-year claim window," whichever is intended.
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the annual benefit-year cycle, or something else.

findings.evidence: "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Use "equipment catalog" consistently instead of introducing "approved list" as a separate term.
findings.violation: "The approved list" appears to refer to the same thing the rest of the document calls the "equipment catalog," but the inconsistent naming makes it unclear whether these are the same artifact.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Specify what "the missing item" refers to, e.g., "until the missing documentation is submitted."
findings.violation: "The missing item" has no clear referent - the document never specifies what items are required at submission time versus what might be missing (receipt? documentation? equipment itself?).

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: State explicitly which request types need more than a photo, or remove the qualifier if a photo is always sufficient.
findings.violation: "Most requests" is vague and doesn't identify which requests require more than a photo or what the additional requirement would be.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person ("You," "we") voice, breaking from the third-person voice ("Employees," "The manager") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" or replace with a neutral transition like "Additionally."
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this sentence follows logically from the prior one about equipment condition checks, but the device-per-category rule is unrelated to that topic.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee" vs. "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."
findings.fix: Clarify whether employees get one claim total per benefit year or one claim per equipment category, and reconcile the two statements.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions, second paragraph vs. Eligibility, first paragraph
findings.violation: These two rules conflict - one implies a single claim per year total, the other implies multiple allowed claims (one per category), without clarifying how categories interact with the single-claim limit.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Either rename the section to reflect its actual content (a process description) or replace it with actual term definitions, and standardize on third-person voice.
findings.violation: Despite the heading "Terminology Notes," this section defines no terms - it describes a process, and it also reintroduces the second-person voice inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for this record throughout the document, or clarify that they are distinct.
findings.violation: "Request log" appears to be a different name for the "reimbursement log" mentioned in Program Overview, but it's not clear if these are the same record or two separate ones.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this redundant paragraph or merge any new information into the "How to Apply" section.
findings.violation: This restates information already covered in "How to Apply" and "Program Coordination" without adding new content, and still uses the inconsistent second-person voice.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Align "Request Steps" with the sequence described in "How to Apply" and "Approval Timeline," or merge these sections to avoid duplicate, conflicting step lists.
findings.violation: This contradicts "How to Apply," which states the process begins with starting a request in the portal (draft, then confirmation summary, then submit) - it never mentions "confirming eligibility" as a first step, and receipt upload timing conflicts with "Approval Timeline," which implies documentation can arrive after submission.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Designate a single owner and a single update cadence for the equipment catalog and use it consistently across all sections.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Program Overview, which attributes equipment catalog updates to "the IT asset group" on "the first business day of the month," creating contradictory claims about who maintains the catalog and how often.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Identify one party responsible for issuing payment and one consistent timing, and remove or reconcile the conflicting statements in the other sections.
findings.violation: This conflicts with "Reimbursement Amounts" ("The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle") and "Terminology Notes" ("Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review") - three different entities (benefits team, finance office, payroll) and two different timeframes ("next pay cycle" vs. "within one pay cycle") are given for who pays out the stipend and when.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the department approver and the manager in "Approval Timeline" are the same role, or describe how they relate.
findings.violation: It's unclear whether "the correct approver" is the same "manager" referenced in "Approval Timeline," leaving the approval chain ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Fold the finance office's $200 threshold review into the "Approval Timeline" section so the full approval sequence and its timing are described in one place.
findings.violation: This additional review step is not integrated into "Approval Timeline," which describes only the manager's two-business-day review, leaving the overall approval timeline incomplete and the two sections inconsistent about what gates payout.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence if only one claim per year is permitted, or clarify the circumstances under which a repeat request could legitimately occur.
findings.violation: This contradicts the Eligibility section's rule that "the stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year," since a repeat request within the same quarter shouldn't be possible if only one claim per year is allowed.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate all equipment catalog ownership/timing statements into a single, consistent description in one place in the document.
findings.violation: This is a third, conflicting claim about equipment catalog ownership (after "IT asset group" in Program Overview and "finance liaison" in Special Cases) and repeats the "start of the fiscal year" timing that conflicts with Program Overview's "first business day of the month."
